title: Favorite clarinetists and influences
summary: He names Jimmy Dorsey-era players on records, says everyone is influenced, and credits Leon Rappolo and Sidney Arodin.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Oh, when the machine was off we were talking about some of your favorite clarinet players on records.
Oh, in the old times, Jimmy Darcy at one time and Don Murray.
Who did you hear them with?

Well, Don Murray with Big Spider-Bag I believe it was and Jimmy Darcy with Red Nichols on some of the records. I had quite a collection of records but when I went to New York and it seems like when I get back from New York they've all gone. It was one of those things, you know, the family didn't take care of them, they didn't see any value to them. The kids played with them and broke them and things like that.
Do you think any clarinet players influenced you much?

Yeah, well anybody, everybody is influenced by somebody else. Although I never did try to copy anybody's style, you subconsciously play like somebody else or like more than one individual, you hit things that you like that somebody else plays and you're going to imitate it without trying to. Rap, for instance, was a great influence on most clarinet players in his time, late Leon Rapolo. He influenced a lot, Sidney Ayrton influenced a lot of clarinet players. He played wonderfully.
A lot of things I hear him do I hear on records by other guys, I think. Oh yeah. I think the Chicago guys picked something from him.

He originated that false fingering on clarinet. And when I was at Nick's in New York, Nick used to tell me that his two favorite clarinet players were Sidney Ayrton and myself, because Sidney had worked there for quite a while. And well, Fasola he went without saying, you know, everybody liked him.
